name: Centre Historique
tagline: The surviving half-timbered streets around Sainte-Anne
description: The medieval quarter that escaped the 1720 fire, a dense grid of leaning timber-framed houses around Place Sainte-Anne and Rue Saint-Michel, which is the city's densest run of bars. The market at Les Lices is a short walk. Everything the city offers socially is inside this square kilometre.
bestFor: Stays that want the bars, the market and the metro all within five minutes
pros: The bar street and the Saturday market both on foot
Metro stations at either end of the quarter
cons: Loud until late every term-time night
The highest rents in the city
Old buildings with thin walls and no lifts

name: Thabor and Jeanne d'Arc
tagline: Around the botanic park, the city's most settled address
description: The eastern districts around the Parc du Thabor, a formal garden and arboretum that is the best public space in Rennes, with nineteenth century stone apartment buildings and quiet residential streets. It is a ten-minute walk to the centre and considerably calmer once you get home.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a park at the end of the street and quiet nights
pros: Ten minutes on foot to the centre

name: Villejean and Beaulieu
tagline: The two university campuses, where the students live
description: The campus districts west and east of the centre, Villejean holding the humanities and medical faculties and Beaulieu the sciences, each with halls, cheap eating and its own metro or bus links. Rents here are the lowest in Rennes and the population is overwhelmingly under twenty-five.
bestFor: Budget stays plugged into the student calendar
pros: The cheapest rents in the city
University canteens, libraries and sports facilities
Metro line to Villejean, direct buses to Beaulieu
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the historic centre

name: Sud-Gare
tagline: The new district around the TGV station
description: The area south of the railway, redeveloped around the high-speed station that puts Paris ninety minutes away, with new apartment buildings, offices and the city's growing technology employers. It is modern rather than charming, well connected on both metro lines, and the flats are the newest in Rennes.
bestFor: People who need the Paris train and want a modern, well-insulated flat
pros: TGV to Paris in ninety minutes from the doorstep
cons: Little character and a lot of construction

name: Vilaine Quays and Bourg-l'Eveque
tagline: Along the river and the canal, west of the centre
description: The districts following the Vilaine and the Ille-et-Rance canal northwest of the centre, with towpath walking and cycling that runs for kilometres, a mix of older housing and newer blocks, and a quieter feel. The centre is a ten-minute walk or a short ride along the water.
bestFor: Stays that want the towpath as a running route and the centre close
pros: Canal and river paths for running and cycling
Ten minutes from the centre on foot
cons: Housing quality varies street to street
Some traffic on the main routes west
